newsitem.title: USA: Dow tumbles more than 200 points as bond rates soar.
newsitem.headline: Dow tumbles more than 200 points as bond rates soar.

text.p: Stocks tumbled on Friday, hurt by weakness in the bond market and rising long-term interest rates that pointed to renewed investor worries about inflation.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell 205.09 points, or 2.5 percent to 7,982.91 shortly after 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT). The index lost more than 100 points right after the market opened, regained some ground, then retreated again as bond prices fell further, driving bond yields higher.

"With the bond market off that much, everybody has to recalculate the cost of borrowing, the cost of money and the cost of holding positions," said Doug Meyers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.

Bond prices began falling on Thursday, after a mixed market reaction to the U.S. Treasury's auction of $10 billion of 30-year bonds. The 30-year Treasury fell 1-25/32, or $17.8125 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.66 percent from 6.53 percent Thursday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Stock investors got spooked when the bond's yield pushed above 6.50 percent, analysts said.

The rising bond yields created anxiety before reports due next week -- including consumer and producer price data and a national retail sales report -- that will give investors further insight into economic growth and inflation.
"There has been a fairly significant shift in sentiment," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"People are thinking the upcoming numbers will paint a picture of faster economic growth than they did two weeks ago. That raises the risk of inflation pressures and higher interest rates."

Federal Reserve policy-makers are to meet on Aug. 19 to consider their next move on rates. They raised short-term rates on March 25, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation, but have held them steady since.

Federal Reserve governor Susan Phillips said on Thursday that growing wage pressures in the economy may point to higher inflation. While higher wages were not fuelling inflation yet, she said, she hinted the central bank was watching closely and was ready for a pre-emptive strike inflation if needed.
The inflation worries boosted gold. The spot August gold contract rose $5.10 to $326.60 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.
"The equity market is taking its cues from the long end of the yield curve," Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division, said.
Selling was widespread and other market gauges also tumbled. The Nasdaq composite index fell 37.29 points to 1,586.89.
Declining issues swamped advancers by 25-3 on active New York Stock Exchange volume of about 332 million shares.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 25.23 points to 925.96.
The American Stock Exchange index lost 8.78 to 643.29.
